source_chain.finding: The restricted filesystem route constructs the trusted inner helper, builds bwrap arguments, and uses run_bwrap_with_proc_fallback. Existing direct full-disk and legacy paths are different and must not be silently changed.

The ordinary no-synthetic/no-protected-target route directly execs bwrap. Existing terminate_with_parent(getpid before fork) is only in the separate synthetic/protected-create cleanup-child branch; it does not provide the inner namespace reaper with a post-exec stable parent reference.

Every bwrap launch adds --as-pid-1. System launcher is preferred when required capabilities are supported; system and bundled exec paths preserve only explicitly owned files by clearing CLOEXEC before exec.

Inner stage verifies zero effective/permitted capabilities, activates any proxy routes, applies the original restrictions, then forks the command and acts as the signal-forwarding waitpid(-1) reaper. It does not currently establish a new parent-death signal or check a stable reference to the pre-exec parent.

Two original tests require command PPID1, namespace PID1 Seccomp2 and equal inherited+1 filter counts; a third requires a real orphan proc entry to disappear. Removing --as-pid-1 would change this security/reaping contract.

bwrap.finding: Upstream0.11.1 sets SIGKILL parent-death in monitor and again immediately before final exec. --new-session calls setsid. With --as-pid-1 it omits its own PID1 reaper. Monitor closes extra descriptors only in its own copy; inherited descriptors are already passed to child.

apparmor.finding: A specific confined profile transition in apparmor_bprm_committing_creds clears pdeath_signal. This demonstrates a possible exec mechanism; it is not evidence that this host took that transition.

manuals.claim: Signal is for subsequent creator-thread death; no retroactive signal if relevant parent/subreapers already died. Fork and specified credential/exec changes can clear it.
A parent outside the current PID namespace is reported as PPID0; terminating namespace init causes kernel SIGKILL of its remaining processes.
A pidfd is a stable task reference, born CLOEXEC, pollable on exit/reap. Process pidfd is available since Linux5.3; plain proc directory fd is not a pollable substitute.

reject: Drop --as-pid-1 and use an unfiltered bwrap PID1
Only PR_SET_PDEATHSIG in inner followed by getppid==0
Modify host LSM profiles or disable restrictions
Plain parent PID polling or scanning unrelated processes

minimal_direction.conditional_on: Use original temporary GET/kill diagnostics to distinguish the actual failure first. This is a concrete design direction, not an accepted production fix or a claim of observed root cause.
minimal_direction.capture: At the final exec_bwrap invocation, after any synthetic/protected-create fork, open pidfd for getpid() itself. That same process becomes the outer bwrap monitor. Self-open avoids a getppid-to-pidfd identity-reuse race.
minimal_direction.placement_constraint: Do not open the pidfd in build_bwrap_argv or before the cleanup supervisor fork: then it would identify an ancestor supervisor instead of the actual inner reaper's direct bwrap parent, leaving an early bwrap-death race.
minimal_direction.role_constraint: Make the trusted-inner-reaper launch role explicit at private call sites. The /bin/true preflight has no inner helper and must not receive the new hidden lifecycle argument. Avoid interpreting untrusted final-command argv as launcher metadata.
minimal_direction.inheritance: Carry the owned pidfd through the already existing preserved_files chain in both system and bundled launchers. Upstream bwrap's monitor closes its own descriptor copy; the sandbox child keeps the passed reference. No writable filesystem mount, PATH, capability or loader change is needed.
inner_sequence: Parse only the private constructed lifecycle FD for the trusted inner stage; reject invalid/missing required input before command execution.
Own the FD immediately and restore CLOEXEC defensively; preserve all existing capability and policy validation.

Establish SIGKILL parent-death for the current direct parent, then perform a zero-time poll of the captured stable pidfd. Readable or HUP means original bwrap is already dead and the namespace init must exit; poll failure/ERR/NVAL fails closed.
Only a live result permits proceeding. Close the pidfd before the final untrusted command fork/exec; do not expose it to user code.

Prove no later exec/credential-changing operation in the reaper can clear this re-established relationship before its wait loop. Current nonproxy chain is capget plus restrictions then fork; preserve proxy path qualification separately.
race_argument: If original bwrap dies during exec or before re-arm, the captured pidfd stays observable as exited even if the namespace reaper has reparented and sees PPID0.
If it dies between re-arm and poll, SIGKILL or the poll readiness prevents admission.
If it dies after a live poll while the unchanged direct-parent relationship remains, the re-established parent-death signal terminates namespace init and the kernel terminates descendants.

This argument depends on the captured FD really coming from the private final-launch constructor, its preservation through bwrap, and no later signal-clearing transition; arbitrary caller-supplied numeric FD is not authenticated parent identity.
compatibility: pidfd_open ENOSYS/EPERM or blocked syscall requires an explicit fail-closed error or separately reviewed compatible mechanism; no silent unsafe fallback.
This adds a Linux5.3 API dependency on the selected route; actual supported-kernel policy and original platform tests must be checked before adoption.
Polling needs no /proc mount, so it can retain the original no-proc fallback contract.
A simple inherited pipe whose write end is only held by bwrap is unsuitable without further ownership: monitor_child closes extra descriptors while still alive.
not_claimed: Full application-parent-to-outer-bwrap startup death guarantee before bwrap's own registration
General support for arbitrary manual --apply-seccomp-then-exec arguments
Actual fixed behavior or root-cause confirmation
B16 authority or Windows sandbox qualification

required_controls.requirements: Same feature graph/helper epoch, original5s marker oracle,0retry, full raw/JUnit; both inner helper and command must actually terminate.

Real owned launcher/namespace/exec chain; hold inner before arm, terminate exactly its captured launcher identity, release owned gate, require no untrusted-command admission and no remaining owned inner. Same control without stable poll must exhibit the early-parent-death hole. No generic timeout counts as cause.
Preserve exact original bodies and assert namespaces actually available; early skip messages do not qualify these contracts.

Real FD must be closed before command; wrong/closed FD fails before admission; both normal and cleanup-fork routes identify the actual bwrap process; preflight unchanged. System/bundled qualification is distinct.
